title: Memory in LLVM IR: alloca, getelementptr, and mem2reg
brief: Count memory instructions, watch mem2reg remove them, then write IR that swaps through pointers, sums an array, reads a struct field, and keeps a variable in an alloca.
hints: In count_opcodes, skip everything outside a `define ... {` / `}` pair, skip label lines (they end with a colon), and take the first word after `%name = ` as the opcode. Lines without an equals sign, such as `store` and `ret`, start with the opcode.

mem2reg_report needs only three calls: cputools.c_to_ir(src, opt="-O0"), cputools.run_opt(ir, "mem2reg"), and your count_opcodes, which you keep only for the four opcodes alloca, load, store, and phi.
swap_ir: load both values first, then store them crosswise. `%x = load i32, ptr %a` reads through a pointer; `store i32 %x, ptr %b` writes through one.
sum_array_ir: `getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %a, i64 %i` is the address of element i. The index needs type i64, so `sext` the i32 loop counter, or count with an i64 from the start.
get_b_ir: the struct type is `%Point = type { i32, i64 }`. `getelementptr inbounds %Point, ptr %p, i32 0, i32 1` is the address of field 1. LLVM, not you, works out that it sits at byte offset 8.

local_sum_ir: make `%s` and `%i` with `alloca i32` in the entry block, store the starting values there, and in the loop load, add, and store back. No phi is allowed to appear: the alloca is the variable.
